answer: Bandwidth-Gated Routing Bottlenecks. The network enforces transmission limits on nodes that frequently wander across dense cluster boundaries. When an agent attempts to route data, it must include a rolling cryptographic cipher derived from real-time path latency and local buffer usage. An attacker trying to forge thousands of distinct cluster nodes faces prohibitive hardware requirements, because each fake identity must independently sustain high-frequency cryptographic challenge-response cycles without dropping packets under load.
